rulings.Case Title: IDIR ZIANI VS. SAMIR RAJIC ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion To Consolidate Cases
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, 2025, Line 5. Plaintiff Idir Ziani's unopposed Motion to Consolidate Case Number CGC-25-631506 with Case Number CGC-25-626252 is GRANTED. The two actions at issue are Ziani v. Rajic, Case No. CGC-25-631506 and Rajic v. Ziani, Case No. CGC-25-626252. Both cases relate to the same vehicle collision. Plaintiff Ziani moves to consolidate the actions under Code of Civil Procedure section 1048(a). Subdivision (a) provides: "When actions involving a common question of law or fact are pending before the court, it may order a joint hearing or trial of any or all the matters in issue in the actions; it may order all the actions consolidated and it may make such orders concerning proceedings therein as may tend to avoid unnecessary costs or delay." When ruling on a motion to consolidate the court should consider the common issues of law and fact, timeliness (trial date/discovery), complexity of the cases, and prejudice to the parties. "There are two types of consolidation: a complete consolidation resulting in a single action, and a consolidation of separate actions for trial. Under the former procedure, which may be utilized where the parties are identical and the causes of action should have been joined, the pleadings are regarded as merged, one set of findings is made, and one judgment is rendered. In a consolidation for trial, the pleadings, verdicts, findings and judgments are kept separate; the actions are simply tried together for the sake of convenience and judicial economy." (Sanchez v. Superior Court (1988) 203 Cal.App.3d 1391, 1396.) Ziani does not clearly identify the type of consolidation sought. Consolidation into one action for all purposes is granted. The parties are identical and the causes of action should have been joined. While the parties should have sought consolidation sooner, it is not necessarily too late to consolidate for all purposes. The cases are consolidated for all purposes. Rajic v. Ziani, Case No. CGC-25-626252 is the lead case. The parties must revise the caption accordingly.
